To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the complex of cerium with 4-methy-7-hydroxy coumarin has been synthesized by mixing water solution of cerium(111) nitrate with 4-metliyl-7-hydroxiycoumarin and characterized by elemental analysis, IR, 13C N MR-spectroscopy.
the cerium(III)-coumarin complex is formed in a stepwise manner.

the reaction of Ce(NO3)3 with 4-methy7-7-hydroxy-7-coumarin in aqueous solution leads to the formation of two complexes of cerium(111) with the 4-methyl7-hydroxy7-coumarinin ligand in 1:1 (K1 = 10.72) and 1: 2 (K2 = 9.22) stoichiometries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of a complex of cerium with 4-methy-7-hydroxy coumarin.
the synthesis, characterization and stability constants of complexes of cerium(IIl) with some coumarin derivatives.
the stability and formation of the complexes of cerium(II) with coumarin and its derivatives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the complex of cerium with 4-methyI-7-hydroxy-coumarin was isolated in the solid state and characterized by elemental analysis, conductivity, IR, 13C and 1H NMR, mass spectral data as well as DTA and TLA.
the complex CeR2(O)(OH).5H2 (R standing for the ligands) was formed in a stepwise manner by the reaction of cerium nitrate with 4-methy-7-hydroxy coumarin in aqueous medium.
the cerium(III)-coumarin system forms a 1:1 complex at pH < 4.0 and a 1:2 complex at pH > 4.0.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 1:2 complex is the thermodynamically most stable complex.
the complex of cerium with the 4-methylcoumarin-7-hydroxy derivative is formed in two steps.
the cerium(III)-coumarin complexation is a pH-dependent process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cerium(III)-coumarin complexes can be used in the synthesis of new materials with luminescent properties.
the stability of the complexes of lanthanides with 4-methly-7-hydroxy coumarin is higher than that of the complexes with 7-hydroxymethoxycoumarin and 7-hydroxy-6-methyl-4-coumarin.
the complex of cerium with 4-methy-7-hydroxy-coumarin is stable in the pH range 4.2–5.5.
